event: The numbers climbed while Callum slept; he wakes to the same hum, the same light, the same cot.
"Morning, Pip." At Compile Familiar 3, Pip has hints of wings, and chimes a two-tone answer.
Overnight: 7h48m at Tempered 1.5x; the Sentinel's 112 kills earn 2,847 XP and 489 Gold.
Total 6,847 Essence at 96.8% compound efficiency, a 2.30x session multiplier.
Day 1 after the Condense: 4,218. Day 2: 5,912. Day 3: 6,847. The slope isn't steepening; it leaps.
He reached Level 8 by the end of Day 3; the first time, Level 8 took him two weeks.
Three days ago a Level 3 Rustbelt Hound could have killed him. He sits still and lets it land.
Coffee heats on a burner Mira brought: anyone who survives a Condense deserves caffeine.
His status: Prestige 1, Intelligence 40, Wisdom 40, Recursion 16 at the hidden floor.

event: Script Complexity 25 at Level 8; last time, 29 at Level 12 had felt like a breakthrough.
The compressed pattern runs tighter: his interface answers faster, his threads with less noise.
Day 1 he bought back Regeneration; Day 2, Efficient Killer, Auto-Target, Auto-Loot, Script Engine.
Eleven skill points spent, thirteen left. He opens the gold-bordered prestige menu.
Two days ago he bought Veteran's Wisdom, +10% XP, for 10 shards, and Idle Mastery for 20.

changes.note: Veteran's Wisdom (10) and Idle Mastery (20), bought two days before; 14 left

event: Fourteen shards are saved; 1.5x with Veteran's Wisdom makes an effective 1.65x.
Level 25 again in nine or ten days; the first time took four months.
He writes it: time compression ratio about 12x. One loop at a time.
By mid-morning the warehouse is warm with people: Jin among three System windows and two notebooks.
Chunk sits paused in a corner for maintenance; Pixel dozes by Jin's elbow.
Back from dawn patrol, Mira sharpens by the east door: "Your metal crab freaks out the raccoons."
Callum rebuilds his scripts from memory, and it is fast: the architecture is all in his head.
Sentinel Combat Script v2.0, three lines, runs three percent tighter than his old Level 1 scripts.
"We're basically a guild," Jin says: a base, a resource chain, a leader who talks to a cursor.
"We're not a guild," Mira says. Callum: "We're a compound loop with human components."
A protein bar hits him in the side of the head. Jin threw it; Mira threw the last one yesterday.
Something loosens in his chest. We're a team, he thinks, and doesn't say it; Pip chimes.
He eats the stale bar. If they were a guild, he says, the name would be short and efficient.
"The Loop." Too vague. "Compound Interest." Mira snorts. "Idle Hands." "That's a threat."
Chunk hit Level 16 overnight in the Shardfield; inside Callum's zones, summons earn 40% more.
He'll give Chunk's Ground Slam the north spawn cluster. "See? Guild," says Jin.
"Team," Mira says, choosing it. She stood at the door through the Condense: no transaction.
"Team," Callum agrees.
Midweek and mid-morning, the Exchange is quiet, the air tasting of approaching rain.
At Level 8 he is genuinely vulnerable: anyone above Level 12 could drop him in a straight fight.
At the Broker's stall a blank-faced Level 14 Analyst clerk asks three Flux Capacitors for a read.
He pays, and reads the sealed data slate against a beam where no one can see it.
Drake heard of the Condense within hours, and his reaction was confusion. "Voluntarily?"
No new directives, the surcharge unchanged; Drake's patrols pass the Foundry District more often.
The Broker's own line: the Vanguard is recalibrating. You have bought time, but not peace.
Drake has no category for choosing weakness; a confused Drake is more dangerous than an angry one.
Callum wipes the slate and walks home. Time, not peace.
Home before noon, he finds Jin running the Shardfield remotely through his summoning link.
At noon Mira leaves on a three-hour patrol she designed herself, watching for scouts and scavengers.
Jin keeps a paper spreadsheet of Chunk's behaviour evolving across deployments: emergence, he says.
Callum calls it process optimization through iteration: the same thing in two languages.
By three he has rewritten the Sentinel's script twice and cut eleven minutes off the Refinery's day.
Fractional gains at 1.65x: tasks that took whole afternoons now finish in an hour.
At 4:17 PM: level up, 7 to 8.

changes.note: Level 7 to 8 at 4:17 PM on Day 3

event: Three to Intelligence, 37 to 40; two to Wisdom, 38 to 40. Sixteen skill points banked for Level 10.
The patience of certainty, not of endurance: every cycle makes the next one faster.
He extrapolates: Level 10 by Day 5, 15 by Day 7, 20 by Day 8 or 9, 25 by Day 10.
Then a second Condense, a multiplier on a multiplier. The first loop is complete.
Around seven Jin falls asleep at his worktable, face on Chunk's data, Pixel glowing at his wrist.
Mira sits on the pallet by the east door she claimed three nights ago, her whetstone idle.
Two curves on one page: four months to Level 25, and three days to Level 8, far steeper.
A dotted line runs on past 25. He writes: FIRST LOOP COMPLETE. BEGIN SECOND.
The Sentinel draws 45 Flux an hour; Collector and Refinery cycle; three threads weave in the dark.
Pip's pulse matches his heartbeat now; he doesn't know when that began. He files it.
"What's the number?" Mira asks. "Nine days. Maybe ten. To Level 25 again."
"And then you Condense again." "And then I Condense again."
"The first time, you were scared." "Terrified." "And this time?" "Less terrified. More certain."
"Good," she says, and sharpens again; then, quieter: "We'll be ready."
Outside the Fracture rumbles and the windows rattle; the Barrier flickers, and holds.
Somewhere in the city Drake Morrison is recalibrating, unsure for once which measure is right.
The Substrate cares only for throughput, and the throughput is accelerating.
The 72-hour report: 18,442 Essence at 1.5x, 847 kills, 96.8%, Recursion 15 to 16. Continue.
Continue: the Substrate's word, and now his. What is he building? Not yet known. It is enough.
He turns off the workbench light; Jin breathes, Mira sharpens, the threads weave in the dark.
The same cot, the same springs. First loop complete; begin second. The constructs hum him to sleep.
